bytes_per_token.description: Divisor converting the token budget into a byte budget. Deliberately a fixed estimate rather than a real tokenizer: a guardrail that is stable across models beats one that is accurate for one of them.

profile_token_budget.description: Token ceiling for the agent-mode profile.

EvidenceTier.description: Evidence strength for a claim, as graded in `docs/metric-families.csv`.

oneOf.description: Published validation, narrower population or weaker linkage.
Weak or contested on its own.
Critiqued; not to be used as a headline.
Novel and unvalidated. Motivated by evidence, not yet supported by it.

HistoryPolicy.description: History window for process metrics. Part of the process `measurement_regime`.

window_days.description: Days of history the process family reads. Stamped into the process `measurement_regime`, so changing it makes old and new numbers incomparable rather than silently different.

count_context_informational.description: Whether context-informational findings advance the counter. Default `false`: an agent must not burn its budget on what it cannot fix.

iteration_cap.description: Passes around the loop before `escalate_to_human`. A policy field, never a constant in the verdict code.

PerfPolicy.description: Latency budgets. Here rather than in the perf harness so that changing one is a ledgered policy edit and not a quiet ratchet (PREMORTEM T6).

fast_lane_cold_cap_ms.description: Cold cap on when a content engine may start (APPROACH graft 4). Enforced while `[sandbox] enabled` switches the async lane on: past the cap the remaining content engines spill to that lane and the record says so. With the lane off — the default — the cap is unenforced, which is the pre-P7 behaviour and the rollback path.

fast_lane_warm_fallback_p95_ms.description:
Warm-cache p95 target for the dirty-tree path with **no** watching fsmonitor daemon.

A second budget rather than a second-class one. Builtin fsmonitor is absent on Linux and can decline anywhere, so the un-accelerated arrangement is what a real fraction of users run — and on a 100k-file repository it costs the best part of a second more than the accelerated one. Holding it to the headline budget would mean either a red gate on every Linux run or the number quietly not being gated at all, and the second is what happened: 1306.9 ms went unreported against a 1000 ms figure the gate was passing.

So it is disclosed, gated, and separate. Raising either is a ledgered policy edit; the gap between them is the cost of not having a daemon, and it is meant to be visible.

fast_lane_warm_p95_ms.description: Warm-cache p95 target for the fast lane, with a watching fsmonitor daemon. The headline number.

max_git_spawns_per_measure.description: Asserted, not observed: a regression that doubles git spawns shows up here before it shows up as latency on someone else's machine.

claim_budget.description: Enforced count. Exceeding it fails the lint, and therefore the build.

max_claims_expiring_per_month.description: Expiry stagger bound, enforced by the lint.

SandboxPolicy.description:
The code-exec lane (PLAN P7, Codex #19).

Everything here is off or empty by default: the async lane is feature-flagged (`enabled` is the flag, and the P7 rollback path), and the only v1 code-exec occupant — the user's own test command — exists only where an operator declares one. A repository that never touches this section measures exactly as it did before the lane existed.

enabled.description: The async lane's feature flag. While `false`, no code-exec engine joins a measurement and the fast lane never spills work to the async lane — `perf.fast_lane_cold_cap_ms` goes back to being unenforced, which is the pre-P7 behaviour and the rollback path.

env_allow.description: Environment variable names passed through to the suite beyond the base allowlist (`andon-sandbox` documents the base list). Default-deny is the rule: nothing else crosses, so secrets in the invoking environment never reach repository code.

memory_limit_mb.description: Best-effort memory cap for the suite's process tree, in MiB. `None` means no cap. Best-effort by name because the mechanisms differ per OS (job-object limit on Windows, address-space rlimit elsewhere) and neither is a security boundary.

test_command.description:
The user's test command, run by the tests engine inside the sandbox through the platform shell (`sh -c` / `cmd /C`). `None` means this deployment ships no code-exec engine at all: the tests engine is absent from the expected-engine roster, not present-and-failing.

Declared here rather than taken as a flag so that the command is policy: the verifier reads it from the base commit, and editing it inside the change under measurement surfaces as a `policy-change` finding (the trusted-command half of Codex #19).

test_timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock cap on the test command, in milliseconds. At the cap the whole process tree is killed and the engine reports a timeout — which is an unanswered question (`engine-unavailable`), never a test failure.

oneOf.description: The rule: measure with the last attested release, so a broken detector cannot bless its own fix.
The bootstrap exception: legal only until the first attested release exists (decision log, 2026-08-16).

binary.description: Which binary is allowed to measure this repository.

excluded_paths.description: Paths excluded from self-measurement — the adversarial fixtures, which exist to fire the tamper suite and would otherwise block every build. Declared here rather than hidden in the runner, so the exclusion is reviewable and the drift signal has something to compare against.

exclusion_drift_signal.description: Emit a finding when the excluded set grows. An exclusion list that quietly widens is how dogfood circularity stops being visible.

Severity.description: Finding severity. "MED+" throughout the plan means `Medium` or above.

oneOf.description: Reported for context; never acted on.
The bottom of the MED+ band.
A strong finding on a diff-actionable metric.
Tamper signals and test failures under conservative defaults.

SeverityPolicy.description: What is allowed to stop the line.

block_on_tamper.description: A tamper signal blocks. Conservative default, and the product's point.

max_severity_for_c_tier.description: The strongest severity a C-tier claim may reach. Weak evidence advises.

med_plus_requires_diff_actionable.description: MED+ severity requires a diff-actionable metric. Blocking on something the agent cannot fix is the uninstall loop of PREMORTEM A4.

med_plus_tiers.description: Evidence tiers that may reach MED+ at all.

history.description: History window for the process family.

loop.description: Agent-loop guardrails, including the iteration cap.

perf.description: Latency and spawn budgets, ledgered rather than hardcoded.

registry.description: Evidence-registry governance: claim budget and expiry stagger.

sandbox.description: The code-exec lane: the async feature flag, the sandbox limits, and the user test command (P7).

schema_version.description: Policy schema version. Only `1` is accepted.

severity.description: What may block, and what evidence is strong enough to.
